methods.label: Work backward one day at a time
methods.explanation:
Eating \(20\%\) leaves \(80\%=0.8\) of the jellybeans present at the beginning of that day. To recover a day's starting amount, divide its ending amount by \(0.8\).

The \(32\) jellybeans left after the second day therefore came from
\[
32\div0.8=40
\]
jellybeans at the beginning of that day. Those \(40\) were left after the first day, so the original number was
\[
40\div0.8=50.
\]
Thus the jar originally contained \(\boxed{50}\) jellybeans, choice \(\text{B}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses the complementary percentage and reverses two percentage steps by decimal division.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is recovering an unknown whole from a known percentage of it, applied twice to successive daily amounts. Percentage conversion and division by a decimal support the written backward method.

review.mathematicalCheck: Each day retains 0.8 of its starting amount. Reversing the two steps gives 32/0.8 = 40 and 40/0.8 = 50. Starting with 50 leaves 40 and then 32.
